stem.en: The Arthaśhāstra and the Śhānti Parva both describe a king's duties. What can a historian safely conclude from these texts alone?

text.en: Every king of the period protected his people and gave fair justice.
The authors expected a ruler to protect people and to ensure justice.
Kings wrote these texts to record what they had done.
No king of the period ever failed in his duties.

explanation.en: These texts describe what a king should do, so they tell us about ideas of governance. They do not prove that every king acted in this way.

hints.en: Does a text about what a king should do tell you what a king actually did?
Look for the option that speaks about expectations.
